Similarly, the fact that you have received other job offers strongly increased the likelihood of departure; only 23% of employees predicted to stay reported receiving outside offers, so this stands out as a clear pull factor. Your relatively short time in your current role (1–5 years) also contributed to the prediction of leaving, as most employees the model expects to remain have built longer tenure here.

Taken together, these signals suggest you may be at a natural transition point. The organization should discuss your career goals openly with you and explore whether targeted opportunities, such as expanded responsibilities or clearer advancement paths, could increase your sense of attachment. You may also wish to reflect on what you are seeking in your next chapter.
